transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-02-25 16:00 PST
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Jon Park (Redwood SE), Lena Brooks (Cedar Ridge Head of Security), Marc Dawson (Platform Eng), Priya Patel (PM), Samir Rao (Infra)

[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Alright everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do intros quick and then dive into the security pilot scoping. I'm Ava, I'm the AE on this account, Jon our SE is here to handle the benchmarking and infra bits.
[00:12] Jon (Redwood SE): hi all, hey. I'll be focused on tests, perf, and the VPC setup details.
[00:18] Lena (Cedar Ridge - Sec): thanks, I just want to be clear up front: from our side we need SOC 2 + ISO27001 evidence, SSO via SAML, RBAC for teams, audit logs, and KMS integration.
[00:30] Ava: totally understood, that's what we wanted to scope today — both attestation docs and how the pilot environment will be set up. quick note: we have a redwood-security-pack that includes SOC2/ISO reports, data flow diagrams, and a KMS integration overview. We'll share that after the call.
[00:45] Marc (Platform): good. also, can you confirm whether pilot will be hosted or private? we have PHI-ish workloads and need network isolation.
[00:53] Jon: yes, great question. for the pilot we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) — that gives you a customer-managed VPC peering or a dedicated VPC with private endpoints. We can also do a hosted footprint but with strict egress controls; however for PHI you usually want the VPC/on-prem option.
[01:10] Samir (Infra): if we do VPC, we need steps on key rotation & KMS. do you support customer key import into your HSM?
[01:18] Ava: we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys (HSM-backed). Jon, want to confirm exact flows?
[01:25] Jon: yep. we have two patterns: bring-your-own-kms where we call your KMS for envelope keys, or our managed KMS with customer key wrap. For the pilot, BYOK is doable — we'll need your KMS endpoint and IAM role. note: sometimes the auto-transcription mislabels KMS as K-N-S, but the flow is unchanged.
[01:44] Lena: ok, audit logs: we need request-level logs, token usage, and an immutable alerting trail for any admin changes. retention 1 year at minimum.
[01:54] Jon: we can stream audit logs to your S3 or SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) via secure delivery. retention is configurable; for the pilot we can enable 1y retention. logs include request metadata, model id, route, timestamps, and user/role id when available.
[02:12] Priya (PM): for success metrics, our main things are: 1) latency targets (P50/P95), 2) accuracy/relevance vs current baseline, and 3) no compliance blockers — e.g., SSO works and audit trails verified.
[02:25] Ava: good, let's put concrete numbers. Marc, what latency is acceptable for UI use?
[02:30] Marc: for short prompts (like triage classification) we want p50 < 200ms, p95 < 600ms ideally. throughput: support bursts to 200 QPS. for longer generation tasks we're okay with higher latency but want throughput >= 30 RPS for bulk jobs.
[02:48] Jon: ok that's helpful. for the pilot we'll propose benchmark scenarios: small token prompts (avg 32 tokens), medium (512 tokens), and long (2048 tokens). we'll test at increasing QPS to find SLO curve and switching points for batching.
[03:05] Jon: note — quantization and model selection will affect latency; we'll test both a high-perf quantized variant and a higher-quality fp16 model to show tradeoffs.
[03:14] Lena: also we need to ensure RBAC integrates with our SAML IdP. users should map to roles: analyst, reviewer, admin, and there must be auditable role changes.
[03:25] Ava: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. roles can be mapped from SAML attributes and enforced in the console and API. Jon, we have a small doc for attribute mappings.
[03:36] Jon: yes I'll attach attribute mapping examples. for the pilot we'll enable RBAC with admin/engineer/viewer roles and show how changes appear in the audit stream.
[03:45] Priya: regarding data retention and deletion — we need guarantees that session data can be deleted on demand, and log snapshots for audits.
[03:53] Ava: for the pilot we can configure data retention windows; also we provide runbook steps for on-demand deletion and a snapshot export for auditors.
[04:02] Marc: what about PII/PHI redaction? we may need to demonstrate that sensitive fields are masked prior to logging.
[04:10] Jon: we can enable selective logging where we strip or hash PII fields before sending to audit storage, or send full logs to a private account only. We'll include redaction knobs in the benchmark plan.
[04:22] Lena: encryption in transit and at rest?
[04:24] Ava: TLS encryption in transit always; at rest we use AES-256 and envelope encryption with customer KMS if requested.
[04:32] Samir: ok network setup — what's the typical latency impact of VPC peering vs hosted?
[04:39] Jon: small overhead, usually single-digit ms added. the bigger latency factor is model size and tokenization. for p50 < 200ms on 32-token prompts we recommend a trimmed model (e.g., 1.5-3B family) with optimized kernels; we'll provide a performance-profile spreadsheet.
[04:57] Priya: can you run a regression check? we need to ensure model updates don't cause quality drops vs our baseline.
[05:03] Ava: yes Redwood Optimize includes eval harnesses — we'll run a set of prompts and measure quality/regression. that will be part of the success criteria.
[05:12] Marc: timing — what's the expected timeline for pilot? provisioning to bench to evaluation?
[05:18] Jon: proposed timeline: Week of Mar 1 - provision VPC & access; Week of Mar 8 - run benchmarks (throughput/latency/accuracy); Mar 15 - present results and remediation plan; Mar 22 - finalize pilot evaluation and decide next steps. That fits a 3-4 week pilot.
[05:36] Lena: sounds reasonable. we may need legal to review data processing addendum (DPA) earlier — Ava can you send the DPA with SOC2 docs?
[05:44] Ava: yes, we'll send DPA, SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001 scope, and our KMS/HSM whitepaper. Expect a zip from me tomorrow.
[05:52] Priya: benchmarks — what exact metrics will you provide? we want latency histograms, cost per 1K tokens, and per-route logs.
[05:59] Jon: deliverables from bench: p50/p95/p99 latency per prompt class; throughput curve vs QPS; cost estimate per 1k tokens for each config; and a workbook with raw logs. We'll also provide a short video of the run for context.
[06:15] Marc: one more on audit logs: can they be WORM (immutable) for a retention period?
[06:19] Jon: we can configure S3 with WORM via Object Lock when streaming logs to your bucket, or use your SIEM with immutable retention policies.
[06:29] Ava: ok let's capture open risks: 1) legal sign-off on DPA, 2) infra provisioning lead time, 3) potential perf variance based on model choice.
[06:37] Samir: provisioning could take 3-5 days internal, so we'll aim to start the week of Mar 1 but might slip if approvals slow.
[06:45] Priya: are there any blockers on Redwood side for PHI pilot?
[06:49] Jon: no blockers, we have the private deployment path and BYOK flows; we just need the network and key info from you.
[06:56] Lena: on RBAC, will role changes be auditable in the console and via API?
[07:01] Jon: yes both — every role change emits an audit event with actor, timestamp, and previous state.
[07:08] Ava: ok summary & next steps — we agreed deliverables to send: SOC2/ISO artifacts, DPA, KMS whitepaper (Ava, by 2/26), bench plan (Jon, by 3/4), customer to provision VPC and share access (Samir, by 3/1), product/metrics shared (Priya, by 2/28).
[07:26] Marc: thanks, please also include sample prompts that you'll use so we can verify representativeness.
[07:31] Jon: will do, we'll include prompt sets for short, medium, long.
[07:35] Priya: thanks all, this was helpful.
[07:38] Ava: great, we'll follow up via email and post the success criteria doc in the shared folder.
[07:44] Lena: thanks, looking forward.

Note on transcription: occasional mis-attributions and small word swaps likely (common with Fireflies export).

References mentioned: Redwood Security pack (link sent after call), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared), DPA and attestation zip, KMS/HSM whitepaper.

End of transcript.
